title: Elevation Credit at FloodGuard Renewal Offer
content:
FloodGuard Private Flood Policy — elevation credit on the building premium at the renewal offer.

## Clause

An elevation credit reduces the building premium by the tier's elevation credit percentage when the elevation certificate on file shows the lowest floor at least one foot above base flood elevation and no flood claim payment was issued on the policy within the 120 months before the renewal offer date; by the tier's elevation credit percentage multiplied by 0.5 when the certificate shows at least one foot above base flood elevation and a flood claim payment was issued within those 120 months; and by nothing when the certificate on file does not show at least one foot above base flood elevation.

## Decision matrix

| Elevation certificate on file | Flood claim payment issued on the policy within the 120 months before the renewal offer date | Credit on the building premium |
|---|---|---|
| Shows the lowest floor at least one foot above base flood elevation | None | The tier's elevation credit percentage |
| Shows the lowest floor at least one foot above base flood elevation | At least one | The tier's elevation credit percentage multiplied by 0.5 |
| Does not show at least one foot above base flood elevation | None | No credit |
| Does not show at least one foot above base flood elevation | At least one | No credit |

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

- With a hypothetical tier elevation credit percentage of 10: 10 percent with no flood claim payment in the 120 months; 5 percent with one.
- With a hypothetical tier elevation credit percentage of 15: 15 percent, or 7.5 percent after a flood claim payment in the 120 months.
- A building premium of 800.00 reduced by 7.5 percent is 740.00.
- A flood claim payment issued 121 months before the renewal offer date lies outside the 120 months, so a qualifying certificate earns the full tier percentage.
